I farm the way I have done for years: I start from what worked last year, then I adjust a little by price, water, and how the crop sold. I have 10.1 mu total, and with only 2 people in the house I cannot spread myself too thin, so I will keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation and leave a smaller piece for cotton. I will do 7.0 mu wheat, then the same 7.0 mu goes into summer maize after wheat harvest, and I will keep 3.1 mu in cotton. Around here, if I cut fertilizer too hard, yield drops fast, and that loss hurts more than spending a bit extra on bags of fertilizer, so I will feed the grain crops a bit steadily and keep cotton a little lighter than maize on nitrogen. Since I have well irrigation, I will not let wheat miss its key water, and for maize and cotton I will water when the field really needs it. For seed, I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize because I have seen those do better in nearby fields, and for cotton I will also use an improved type that is easier to manage. Tillage-wise, I will keep it practical: rotary for wheat and cotton to make a decent seedbed, and no-tillage or very light direct seeding for maize after wheat so I do not lose time in summer. I will also keep pesticide sprays to the usual number, because saving one spray can end up costing much more in yield.
